title: The Endpoint That Isn't Actually Busy
summary: Chidi's raw log count says /api/garage is Datacore's busiest endpoint. Almost none of those requests actually succeed.

client.name: Chidi Okafor
brief: This log file has one line per request — method, path, status code, how long it took. /api/garage has way more lines than anything else, so that's where I was about to add more servers.

But I just noticed most of those lines are 500s and 502s — a client out there is stuck retrying something that's failing, not real traffic. Can you write something to count what's actually succeeding?
client.thanks: wallet. I'd have thrown capacity at the wrong service — garage's failures were drowning out the real traffic in a raw count.

starterSql:
# Which endpoint is really getting the most traffic?
# Careful: a failed request (500, 502, 503) still shows up as a line in the log.
#
# access_log is a list of dicts, each with one key: "line" — the raw log line.
# Set a variable named `result` to your answer (the path, as a string).

for row in access_log[:5]:
    print(row['line'])

result = None

tables.name: access_log
tables.description: Raw request log, one line per request: "DATE TIME METHOD PATH STATUS DURATIONms".

hints.title: Hint 1: A log line isn't a success
hints.desc: Every request gets a line, including ones that failed. Split each line on spaces to pull out the path and the status code.

hints.title: Hint 2: Only count the 2xx ones
hints.desc: A status of "200" means it actually worked. Only count a request toward a path's total when its status is "200".

hints.title: Hint 3: Then take the highest count
hints.desc: Once you have successful-request counts per path, `result` is the path with the highest one.

findings.claim: Which endpoint is really getting the most traffic?

options.text: /api/garage — it has by far the most log lines
/api/wallet — fewer total lines, but almost all of them succeed
/api/missions — tied with garage for the most lines

findings.claim: Why did the raw line count point at the wrong endpoint?

options.text: A broken client is stuck retrying a failing request against /api/garage, filling the log with 500s and 502s that aren't real usage.
/api/wallet's requests aren't being logged at all.
It didn't mislead — /api/garage really is the busiest.

successFeedback: /api/garage racks up the most log lines, but most of them are a retrying client's failures, not real use. Once you only count the 200s, /api/wallet is clearly the busiest endpoint.

fixtures.failHint: Your answer doesn't match the endpoint with the most successful (200) requests here.
A flooded endpoint can have the most log lines and still not be the busiest. Only count status 200.

fixtures.purpose: A different day where a different endpoint is flooded with failures
fixtures.failHint: Your answer is wrong on a different day's log — it may be hardcoded to always exclude one path instead of checking the status.
